System 04 / Compact block storage

Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking

Drive-in racking removes the aisles between rack rows so forklifts drive into the racking and place pallets on rails, one behind another. Drive-in works last-in, first-out; drive-through is open at both ends and works first-in, first-out. It stores about 60% to 80% more pallets than selective racking.

How it works

How drive-in / drive-through racking works

Instead of beams, pallets rest on continuous rails on each side of a lane. The forklift drives into the lane and places pallets from the back to the front, so a single lane holds many pallets of the same product.

In drive-in racking the lane is entered from one side only, so the last pallet in is the first out. Drive-through racking is open at both ends, so pallets are loaded on one side and picked from the other.

Is it the right fit?

When to choose drive-in / drive-through racking

  • You hold large quantities of relatively few SKUs
  • Space is expensive, as in cold stores
  • Products are not time-critical, or FIFO is handled with drive-through
  • Pallets are of consistent size and quality

Compare

When another system may fit better

  • Selective pallet racking when you need access to every pallet.
  • Pallet flow racking for strict FIFO with dense storage.
  • VNA racking for density with full selectivity.

Questions

Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking FAQs

What is the difference between drive-in and drive-through racking?

Drive-in racking is entered from one side only, so it works last-in, first-out. Drive-through racking is open at both ends, so pallets are loaded from one side and retrieved from the other on a first-in, first-out basis.

Is drive-in racking suitable for cold storage?

Yes. Cold stores are expensive to build and run per cubic metre, and drive-in racking stores about 60% to 80% more pallets than selective racking in the same space, which makes it a common choice for frozen and chilled goods.

What are the limitations of drive-in racking?

Only the pallet at the front of each lane is accessible, so it suits few SKUs with many pallets each. Forklift drivers work inside the racking, so guidance channels, upright guards and operator training are important.
